title: Quantity of heat
textbookText: Chapter 11 Quantity of heat Henri Victor Regnault was a French chemist and physicist best known for his careful measurements of the thermal properties of gases. He was an early thermodynamicist and was a mentor to William Thomson in the late 1840s. Regnault designed an apparatus for a large number of physical measurements and carefully determined the specific heats of many solids, liquids, and gases. He showed that no two gases have precisely the same coefficient of expansion and proved that Boyle’s law of the elasticity of a “perfect gas” is only approximately true for real gases. In introducing his air thermometer, he determined the absolute expansion of mercury. He also devised a hygrometer.
1. A large iceberg melts at the base but not at the top. 2. Even if you add heat to an object, the temperature of the object may not change.

11.1 Introduction If two bodies are brought in thermal contact then the hotter body cools down and the colder body warms up until they attain equilibrium temperature. During this process, energy is transferred from the hotter body to the colder body. This energy in transit is called heat. The transfer of heat continues whenever the temperature difference exists between two bodies. Therefore, heat is a form of energy and is a scalar quantity. We cannot directly measure the quantity of heat on the body; instead, it can be measured as the quantity of heat transferred from one body to another. The quantity of heat transferred in a process may change the temperature of the body. For a given value of heat exchange, the change in temperature will depend upon the mass of the body and the nature of the material of the body. By knowing the value of the temperature change, mass and specific heat capacity (nature of substance), we can calculate the quantity of heat exchanged by a body. When the thermos flask, which contains a liquid is shaken vigorously, the temperature of the liquid gets raised without supplying heat. A similar phenomenon can be observed in the case of gases. In both cases, work done on the system becomes a source of heat energy.
